newsitem.title: USA: Illinois corn, soybean harvest slowed by rain.
newsitem.headline: Illinois corn, soybean harvest slowed by rain.

text.p: Corn and soybean harvest in Illinois was slowed during the week ended Sunday by widespread rains, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.
Corn was 50 percent harvested, compared to 88 percent last year and the five-year average of 71 percent. Soybeans were 74 percent harvested, versus 97 percent last year and the average of 93 percent.
Much of the corn in the northern districts still has a high moisture content, the report said.
Corn was 98 percent mature versus 99 percent on average. The weekly report said 98 percent of soybean plants were dropping leaves, versus an average of 100 percent.

Wheat seeding reached 77 percent complete compared to 90 percent last year and 86 percent on average. Forty-eight percent was emerged compared with the 61 percent average, the Illinois crop update said.
Sorghum was 31 percent harvested, compared with 67 percent for the five-year average. The crop was 94 percent mature, versus the five-year average of 96 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated 10 percent surplus, 73 percent adequate, 16 percent short and one percent very short.
